---
title: "Register-based research at DST"
subtitle: "Who is this guide for, and what will you learn?"
date: last-modified
---

This guide takes you from a research question to a finished, exportable result
using the Danish registers on the DST server. It assumes no prior register
experience and only a little R.

**New here? Start at [phase 1 - Plan your study](plan-your-study.qmd)** and
follow the phases in order. Working on DARTER (project 708421)? Read [DARTER -
overview and pipeline](darter-index.qmd) first.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Looking for something specific?** Search in the top right. The box matches
exact words; **Search by meaning** next to it also understands synonyms and
Danish, for when you do not know what the thing is called here.
:::

## The phases of the guide

The guide is built as 14 phases, running from planning to export.

  | Phase                                                              | Contents                                                                        |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | [1 - Plan your study](plan-your-study.qmd)                      | Research question, key concepts and data model                                  |
  | [2 - R: the bare essentials](r-intro.qmd)                       | The minimum of R you need to get going                                          |
  | [3 - Log in to DST](log-in-dst.qmd)                             | Access to the server and the first overview                                     |
  | [4 - File types and loading](file-formats.qmd)                  | Parquet and SAS - formats and conversion                                        |
  | [5 - Extracting data step by step](extraction-step-by-step.qmd) | The universal extraction pattern: read_register/open_dataset → filter → collect |
  | [6 - First extraction](first-extraction.qmd)                    | Your first real extraction with synthetic data                                  |
  | [7 - Inspect your data](inspect-data.qmd)                       | Check structure, types and distributions before analysis                        |
  | [8 - Find your registers](find-your-registers.qmd)              | Find the right registers for exposure, outcome and covariates                   |
  | [9 - Hospital contacts (LPR)](understand-lpr.qmd)               | LPR2/LPR3 and ICD codes                                                         |
  | [10 - Build your study population](build-study-population.qmd)  | Cohort, index date, in/exclusion, censoring and special designs                 |
  | [11 - Extract variables](extract-variables.qmd)                 | Extract outcomes, socioeconomics and comorbidity - filtered to the cohort       |
  | [12 - Assemble and prepare the dataset](data-manipulation.qmd)  | Joins, pivots and handling missing data                                         |
  | [13 - Analysis](analysis.qmd)                                   | Tables, figures, regression, time-to-event, rates and sensitivity analyses      |
  | [14 - Export and repatriation](export.qmd)                      | Get your results safely out of DST                                              |

### Look-ups - use as you go

These pages are **not** part of the numbered guide - jump here when you have a
specific question.

  | Page                                                   | Use it when you want to...                                                                         |
  | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | [Search by meaning](search.qmd)                        | find a page by synonym or by the Danish word, when the exact-match box comes up empty              |
  | [Overview of registers](register-reference.qmd)        | find the confirmed column names, types and join keys for each register                             |
  | [Find a variable](find-a-variable.qmd)                 | look up which register a given variable lives in                                                   |
  | [Format tables](formatting-tables.qmd)                 | translate codes to text (municipality, education and employment codes) with DST's SAS format files |
  | [Parquet and fastreg](parquet-and-fastreg.qmd)         | point fastreg at your registers, or convert SAS files to parquet                                   |
  | [Functions: overview](function-guide.qmd)              | look up a single function - what do `filter()`, `collect()`, `%>%`, `left_join()` do?              |
  | [Good coding practice](good-coding-practice.qmd)       | structure, naming and reproducible code                                                            |
  | [DST pitfalls](dst-pitfalls.qmd)                       | check the traps where your code runs and the answer is quietly wrong                               |
  | [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd)                 | work out a red error message, or an empty result, and find where to ask                            |
  | [Algorithms & special packages](packages-overview.qmd) | ready-made algorithms (OSDC, NMI) to derive variables                                              |
  | [Learning resources](learning-resources.qmd)           | courses and books for R, epidemiology and statistics                                               |

Do you have reusable code for register-based research - e.g. a SEPLINE
